title: Parameters and Arguments
learningObjectives: Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: Parameters are variables named in a function signature. Arguments are the expressions supplied when the function is called. Ordinary parameters are passed by value; reference parameters can alias caller data.
understand.whyItMatters: Parameters let a function operate on different inputs without depending on global variables. Reference parameters can avoid copying or intentionally allow modification.
understand.explain: At a call, argument positions correspond to parameter positions. A value parameter receives its own copy. A const reference offers read-only access without copying, while a mutable reference should be used only when modification is intended.

examples.title: Two parameters
examples.code: int add(int left,int right){return left+right;}\n// add(3,4) -> 7
examples.explanation: The two arguments initialize left and right in order.

examples.title: Read-only string reference
examples.explanation: A const reference avoids copying a string and prevents modification through this parameter.

examples.title: Value parameter isolation
examples.code: void setLocal(int x){x=99;}\nint n=5;setLocal(n); // n is still 5
examples.explanation: Changing the local copy does not change the caller's variable.

examples.title: Expression as argument
examples.explanation: An expression is evaluated and its result is passed as an argument.

examples.title: Parameter order
examples.code: int subtract(int a,int b){return a-b;}\n// subtract(9,2) -> 7
examples.explanation: Swapping arguments changes the result because their positions matter.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Parameters and Arguments examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Write a function that accepts a price and tax rate. Compare pass-by-value with a const-reference parameter for a string label. Add a separate reference parameter only when changing caller state is required.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.

questions.explanation: Parameters receive the supplied argument values.
The const reference avoids copying and prevents mutation through it.
Expressions can be evaluated and passed.
